caveats: Small at the surface: in iSWA's samples the dose rate peaks at 1.243 x the 5-day background, below the RAD team's 1.25 x trigger, at a median spacing of 61.6 min. Hassler et al. 2014 write that "its energy spectrum was hard enough to produce an enhancement of ~30% over the GCR dose rate on the martian surface"; the RAD team's Table 1 (Löwe et al. 2025) lists 2013-04-10 as triggered with 9.22 uGy, a row hapi_msl_rad_sep_events does not reproduce.

Three dates for one event: Table 1 prints '2013-04-10', the paper's Fig. 5 caption 'sol 242 (11 to 12 April 2013)' and its Fig. 1 'sol 242 (12 to 13 April 2013)'. In iSWA's samples the dose rate peaks at 2013-04-11T14:19:27Z.

Different instruments, places and quantities: RAD's dose rate in plastic at Gale crater (uGy/day), STEREO-B HET's proton flux per energy bin in interplanetary space (#/(cm2-sr-s-MeV/n)) and NOAA's >10 MeV integral flux at Earth (pfu). No absorbed dose is converted to Sv, and no arrival times are compared.
'The same SEP event' is the paper's claim (its Fig. 5 caption), quoted, not LANDFALL's.
JPL's 2013 windows and quotes are read from horizons_mars_comms, which did not re-fetch the JPL page this build (2013_orbiters, 2013_curiosity: quote read by hand in the raw page HTML).

STEREO-B HET hourly means are LANDFALL's reduction of 10035 one-minute rows; the 14.3 MeV channel reads 0 when quiet, so multiples are given only for 50 and 80 MeV (11,148 x and 1,577 x their 8-9 April medians).

The first clear rise is the first sample above 1.1 x the background (a design choice). The sample before it (2013-04-11T08:11:42Z, 1.043 x) is not taken as the rise: the record reaches 1.043 x again after the event (2013-04-12T21:05:47Z).
pdfminer renders this PDF's µ as 'm' and its ± as 'T', so no µGy or ± figure is quoted from it.
Moratorium counts are samples in iSWA's record inside each published window, not a statement about what was downlinked when.

data.explainer: Sol 242: Curiosity's RAD measured a solar particle event at Gale crater on 11 April 2013, while Mars was in solar conjunction and JPL had planned to suspend commanding to Curiosity. Rebuilt from NASA's public records (MSL RAD on CCMC iSWA, STEREO-B HET on CDAWeb), beside NOAA's list and the RAD team's paper. Nothing here feeds LANDFALL's engine, rules or scenario.

fragments.text: (A) Dose rate enhancement observed on the martian surface by RAD on sol 242 (11 to 12 April 2013), while Mars was in solar conjunction. (B) The same SEP event seen from the STEREO-B spacecraft, almost magnetically aligned with Mars. (C) The same SEP event seen by the GOES-13 satellite in earth orbit, almost 180° away in heliospheric longitude.
STEREO-B was leading Mars (in longitude) at the time of the event and had similar, but not identical, magnetic connection to the Sun.
Because Mars was in solar conjunction at this time, GOES-13 was nearly 180° in heliospheric longitude away
its energy spectrum was hard enough to produce an enhancement of ~30% over the GCR dose rate on the martian surface
The 40- to 100-MeV proton flux seen by STEREO-B
increased almost four orders of magnitude at the peak of this event
The minimum proton energy required to reach the surface in Gale crater is ~150 MeV.
Mars’ Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory’s Curiosity Rover
